fields.sample_size: 585 respondents in open-defecation-free villages of Dantewada district (Chhattisgarh) and Malda and Cooch Behar districts (West Bengal), December 2019-April 2020; questionnaire in local languages with rating scales; Bhutni (West Bengal) has about 3,000 people in six hamlets and 415 households; a bibliometric review of 89 CLTS articles (Scopus, 2015 onward) precedes the survey
fields.effect_measure: covariance-based structural equation modelling (CBSEM) of a hybrid technology-acceptance and theory-of-planned-behaviour model (perceived usefulness, ease of use, facilitating conditions, attitude, subjective norms, continuation of intention, health and hygiene, risk of epidemic diseases); standardised path estimates, AVE and discriminant-validity checks
fields.effect_estimate: Subjective norms and facilitating conditions are the major determinants of continuation of intention to keep using toilets under CLTS, which in turn improves health and hygiene and reduces the risk of epidemic disease spread (the full text gives path estimates and the correlation matrix in Tables 6-8). Context: Dantewada district (about 0.25 million people, more than 75% scheduled tribes) had under 10% sanitation coverage at the launch of Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin in October 2014, reached 40% in a year with 30 trained CLTS facilitators and was declared ODF within 30 months; sanitation coverage in the West Bengal district was 40% before CLTS. The authors conclude that CLTS and the Swachh Bharat Mission reached marginalised tribal communities; no counterfactual or access measure is analysed.
fields.section: Full text (Research Square preprint, 38 pages): Abstract; Literature review (bibliometric analysis); Research methodology 4.1-4.4 (case setting, measurement model, data collection); Results (SEM); Discussion
fields.exact_location: Section 4.4 (data collection, n = 585); Tables 3 and 6-8; Discussion; published version Environ Sci Pollut Res 2022 (doi 10.1007/s11356-022-18854-3)
fields.study_design: cross-sectional survey with structural equation modelling plus a bibliometric literature review (case study of the Swachh Bharat Mission CLTS approach)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a cross-sectional survey (585 respondents) with structural equation modelling of behavioural determinants of CLTS continuation in tribal communities in India; read in full text 2026-10-04 from the preprint version. The exposure is behavioural constructs, not a legal or administrative rule.
